Question 1
?

Calculate ∫log3⁡(2x)x2dx.

a
−ln⁡(2x)+1ln⁡3+C
b
ln⁡(2x)−1xln⁡3+C
c
−ln⁡(2x)+1xln⁡3+C
d
ln⁡(2x)+1x2ln⁡3+C
e
1−ln⁡(2x)xln⁡3+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Use log₃(2x)=ln(2x)/ln(3). Integration by parts with u=ln(2x) and dv=x⁻² dx gives v=−1/x and du=dx/x. Thus the integral is −ln(2x)/(x ln(3))−1/(x ln(3))+C, which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{x})-\int (-\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int -\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Calculate ∫log3⁡(2x)x2dx.

a
−ln⁡(2x)+1ln⁡3+C
b
ln⁡(2x)−1xln⁡3+C

−ln⁡(2x)+1xln⁡3+C

ln⁡(2x)+1x2ln⁡3+C

1−ln⁡(2x)xln⁡3+C

EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log3⁡(2x)⟹u′=1xln⁡3v′=1x2⟹v=∫1x2dx=−1x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫log3⁡(2x)x2dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log3⁡(2x)⋅(−1x)−∫(−1x)(1xln⁡3)dx=−log3⁡(2x)x−1ln⁡3∫−1x2dx=−log3⁡(2x)x−1xln⁡3+C=−ln⁡(2x)xln⁡3−1xln⁡3+C=−ln⁡(2x)+1xln⁡3+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log3⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡3.

content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{x})-\int (-\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int -\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(3{x}^{3})-\int \frac{3{x}^{3}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-3\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{x}^{3}+C \\  & ={x}^{3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫2xlog5⁡(x)dx.

a
 x2ln⁡5(ln⁡x−1)+C
b
 x22ln⁡5(3ln⁡x+2)+C
c
 x22ln⁡5(2ln⁡x−1)+C
d
 x2ln⁡5(4ln⁡x−1)+C
e
 x22ln⁡5(4ln⁡x+1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using log₅(x)=ln(x)/ln(5), integrate by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=2x dx. The result is [x² ln(x)−x²/2]/ln(5)+C=x²(2 ln(x)−1)/(2 ln(5))+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{5}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x{log}_{5}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(x)({x}^{2})-\int ({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}{log}_{5}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}{log}_{5}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{5}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫2xlog5⁡(x)dx.

a
 x2ln⁡5(ln⁡x−1)+C
b
 x22ln⁡5(3ln⁡x+2)+C
c
 x22ln⁡5(2ln⁡x−1)+C
d
 x2ln⁡5(4ln⁡x−1)+C
e
 x22ln⁡5(4ln⁡x+1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log5⁡(x)⟹u′=1xln⁡5v′=2x⟹v=∫2xdx=x2

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫2xlog5⁡(x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log5⁡(x)(x2)−∫(x2)(1xln⁡5)dx=x2log5⁡(x)−1ln⁡5∫xdx=x2log5⁡(x)−1ln⁡5⋅x22+C=x2ln⁡xln⁡5−x22ln⁡5+C=x22ln⁡5(2ln⁡x−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log5⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡5.

content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{5}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x{log}_{5}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(x)({x}^{2})-\int ({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}{log}_{5}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}{log}_{5}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{5}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.$

after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/2}^{1}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)\text{d}x={\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}{log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\cdot 1\cdot \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv{|}_{1/2}^{1}-{\int }_{1/2}^{1}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x){|}_{1/2}^{1}-{\int }_{1/2}^{1}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot 1)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{1}{2})-{\int }_{1/2}^{1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡1-x{|}_{1/2}^{1}\,] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0-(1-\frac{1}{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$
